Immortal Redneck is a first person shooter that has the titular character, a mummified redneck with a penchant for glib one-liners, shooting and cursing his way through three progressively more difficult pyramids filled with ancient Egyptian monsters.It may bear resemblance to games like Quake and Serious Sam at first, but at its core is a set of systems taken wholesale from roguelite action titles like The Binding of Isaac and Rogue Legacy. The game hosts a whole range of features familiar to anyone who's played a roguelite in the last few years; procedural generation, classes, skills, permadeath and a literal upgrade tree.
The game plays very much like a modern take on it's 90's influences. Character movement is fast and there is a mix of enemies that force you to keep it that way. From static ranged attackers who fire projectiles to faster melee based enemies that chase you out of cover. The designs of the enemies are very readable and their behaviours are predictable, which makes the early part of the game deceptively easy. When enemy variety is upped, however, you understand that learning the way the enemies work together and which of them to focus on is important to each encounter.
Enemies regularly drop health, ammo and money which will eventually despawn; this helps to encourage you out of cover and comes right out of the 90s shooter playbook. Guns drop from downed monsters too and there are about 30 to choose from with each having it's own strengths and weaknesses. Enemies might even drop a powerful game modifier presented in the form of a papyrus scroll. The effects of these scrolls range from simple stat boosts to more strategy affecting abilities like immunity to arena traps, damage reflection or the chance to turn enemies into chickens. Oh, and some of these scrolls can be rather less helpful. I was unlucky enough to pick up a scroll that removed all of my previously collected upgrades just before a boss fight. Naturally, you can't tell what a scroll will do until you pick it up which creates the familiar risk/reward gambit. If you've grabbed a couple of useful power ups, you probably won't want to risk losing them.
The layout of the three pyramids is randomly generated from a large pool of hand crafted rooms and there are more than enough of them that the game never feels samey. There's a generous variety of design in each room too and a surprising amount of vertical space in which to explore and, well, shoot at stuff. You're able to climb up ledges from the get go and can later upgrade the amount of jumps you can use. There are occasional secrets hidden in the larger spaces and I suspect there's a lot to learn in Immortal Redneck for anyone looking for a title they'll keep going back to.
As you make your way up each pyramid the floors become smaller and smaller, encouraging as much exploration as you can manage as early as possible so you're better prepared for the more difficult fights towards the top. There are usually a couple of exit rooms on the larger floors and occasionally you will find a reward room with one or more treasure chests in it. These can be freebies but there are a few presented as little challenges. In these rooms enemies don't spawn and instead you're tasked with getting through a gauntlet of jumping puzzles and traps without taking damage. It's a nice way to break up the otherwise relentless pace of high energy gunplay, I like to call this gameplay punctuation. By that measure, a full stop might come in the place of boss fights. There are two in each pyramid, one at the halfway point and another at the top. Each boss will require a different strategy to defeat and they're sufficiently difficult enough that they become choke points for progression.
When you die in Immortal Redneck, your current run is over and you're deposited back to the start with all of the money you've collected. You can spend this money on an upgrade tree, I really do love that it's an actual tree, ripped directly from Rogue Legacy. Here you can boost statistics like health, damage and defence and even unlock a shop and different classes.
Classes offer alternative powers and starting weapons as each class has a passive and active power which can be popped off in the middle of a fight. Again, this plays into that moment-to-moment strategy formulation that is at the heart of the roguelike genre.
Standard roguelike fare with the shop as well; you can buy a few upgrades, shortcuts further into each pyramid and the ability to revisit the pyramid set up you previously visited - albeit without gaining coins again. Once your ready to move on, you can re-enter the pyramid at the cost of your remaining coins.
I'm really enjoying my time with Immortal Redneck and about the only thing I don't like about it is it's main character. Whether or not he's intentionally cast as a foul mouthed doofus is hard to read but those glib one-liners I mentioned before? They rarely hit base. The Immortal Redneck himself may well fit with characters like Duke Nukem and Serious Sam but I never had any fond feelings for those characters either. On top of that, there are a few one liners that seem to be more prone than others to activating. If I have to hear "What's wrong McFly, chick chick chicken" one more time I may throw my computer out the window.
Changing your strategy to account for what skills you have and what enemies you're facing is fundamental to Immortal Redneck and it's ability to take so many design trends from roguelites and apply them to the shooter genre is it's biggest strength. I recommend to anyone looking for their next roguelite fix. It's a polished, fun experience and I'm going to do my best to at least beat the second pyramid.

Where do I begin with Banished... With 120hrs on record, I haven't yet found a rhythm that can help me ascend to the greats and build a town that doesn't fall apart over a small span of time. One second I have more food than... Well, I have a lot of food, and lots of tools and resources and the works, the next minute my citizens are dying off and my town is up in metaphoric flames.
But I think that's the beauty of this game. I've played consistently on either easy/medium difficulty with disasters off, and I *still* can't exhaust the avenues of this game. There's such a learning curve, it's astounding. One day, perhaps when I have 300hrs on record, I'll graduate to turning on natural disaters, but we'll see...
There are some complaints that there isn't much to this game, and I suppose when you look at the 'tech' or the buildings you can produce, that's correct, but the very fact that the game can be so simple in concept and yet so complex in its gameplay and its outcome - shows this game for the gem it really is.
I will admit that some of the negative reviews on here that point out the sometimes frustrating AI have a fair point, but every game has its issues, and I think these downfalls are more than made up for by the beautiful style, gameplay, and concept. Couple this with a beautiful and relaxing soundtrack and you have a game that you can never stay mad at when it kicks you in the teeth and wipes out your town, because it was all down in the picturesque landscape with a soothing track to keep you distracted.
Another comment on here I think perfectly sums up why this game is worth every penny: you can leave this game for months/years at a time (I know, that's how I play it), but then you get the powerful urge/itch to play it, and nothing else will fill that void other than Banished. It is timeless, and I genuinely think it'll be classic in an age when we're looking at countless CoD sequels etc.
The playability is further boosted (if you could boost it any further) by the vast array of mods that open up the possibilities with more buildings and new mechanics. To name but a few, the mods by Redketchup will add at least another 500hrs to your gameplay.
So, I think for the mere price of £15, if you're thinking of getting Banished, think no more, buy it now!

Glacially slow, aimless and obtuse.
The writing is good, but when you die (and the game stresses that you WILL die, often) you effectively restart the game - which means you'll end up reading the same text over and over and over again.  It's not good enough to make this an OK flaw.  (Permadeath isn't a problem with most procedural roguelikes as each play is sufficiently different from the last - that's not the case here, as all that seems to change is that the islands get shuffled a bit, which is nowhere near enough)
Once you get your bearings, this can be fun for a few hours - then you die, and then you have to repeat those exact same hours just to get back to where you were.  The core mechanics outside of the writing are nowhere near strong enough to make up for this (sailing is slow, trading is pointless, combat is dull), so this is where I stopped.
I really wanted to love this, but I didn't.
(The soundtrack is great, though, and I'd recommend buying it separately)

A thought provoking and realistic survival game, you wont find mutants, zombies, dragons or any other unrealistic crap here!
Even in it's current state (no story mode yet, just solo sandbox) I'd compare it with 'The Road' when it comes to the mood and atmosphere. The sound of the wind is your only companion in this game, only to be occasionally interrupted by the spine chilling howl of a wolf, or wolves. This game will scare you, whether you're walking through the forest after a blizzard, exploring abandoned houses or winding your way through the dreaded 'Carter Hydro Dam' (I'll let you play the game to find out why :D) you will be on the edge of your seat. Things can and WILL go 'south' in this game very fast. In my most recent game I was warm, well fed, in perfect health... I decided to go foraging. After a while walking through the snow I came accross a black bear, I had 3 rounds in my rifle, took the shot (I was running low of food stores) but I didn't kill it, I was then mauled and left in the snow to bleed out.
It was my stupid decision but it shows that you have to be so careful in this game. Supplies are scarce, you are your own worst enemy, you have to deal with tiredness, health, hunger, thirst and of course warmth.
I highly reccommend this game, as I said at the start it's thought provoking and has great atmosphere. This game really makes you appreciate the things we often take for granted in our day to day lives.

Story mode offers some incentive to do something and explore. Though the story so far hasn't offered much as motivations are unexplained and vague a few hours in. Maybe it gets better? But I heard the story will be episodic, which is disappointing but I guess they really wanted to finally release the game.
Survival mode offers very little. But if you like the exploration and staying alive for no real reason other than just staying alive, you'll enjoy it. You run between locations to scavenge, most of the time is spent looking through drawers, boxes and other containers but also inside the crafting menues. You work to maintain your sleep, hunger, thirst and the state of your clothing and gear. You also try to find the resources to craft new tools and clothing.
Some times you also get sick or injured, which depending on the severity most likely will kill you or severely exhaust your resources. It adds an unpredictable, random element to the survival that's as much a challenge as a frustration. It's realistic in that regard.
There are bunkers you can find, but to my knowledge that's the only reason you go exploring anywhere special.
That's what this is. While it can be fun to just mindlessly drone away at surviving with no real end goal that's also the games weak point. It's a good game to listen to audiobooks to or watch your favorite TV-series.
It's not good enough to be a thumbs up. It's not really bad either, but since I don't feel I can recommend it I will have to make it a thumbs down.

- The 2x and 3x speed options should be faster
- A campaign mode would be great, with different scenarios in different malls (e.g. low funds, large rat problems, huge funds to turn derelict mall into thriving one, limited builders)
- Possibly a variable difficulty, making it easier to generate profit or starting with a little more cash
- An improved UI is needed, it's a bit messy. I'd personally prefer the menu at the bottom. The tabs 'Build', 'Assign' etc, could go bottom left corner, in a column, and clicking one could open up a bar along the bottom with tabs above to refine (e.g. the tabs above could be for Roadwork, Objects, etc., with all of the choices for each of these categories in the bar below). Then, the little notifications could appear on the left where they would be much more noticeable.
- An advertising option could be useful for increasing customers and profits, even if just for a short time.
Overall, it's a decent game. However, at this early stage, it doesn't warrant a huge amount of playing time as you can leave it on in the background without needing to do anything to generate money, but this takes far too long. Maybe I just haven't done very well!

Superhot is a title that at first, is unique and innovative from many other shooters.
However after playing it for around 7 hours,I enjoyed the game, but there were lots of major problems with it, and through my playtime I managed to pin down 5 major problems
1. Lack of content
The game has 3 different modes, campaign, endless, and challenge.
Endless and challenge are modes that are cool and fun at first, but get boring and can only keep you on for about 1 or 2 hours AT THE MOST for each mode.
Campaign here is probably the main mode of the game and you should probably get it just for that.
And speaking about the campaign...
2. The campaign is WWAAYYYYYYYY to short
The campaign, the main staying point of the game, took me 3 HOURS to FINISH
And I experimented with different things and messed around a lot too!
Most people if they are trying can finish this in 2 OR EVEN 1!!!!!!
And the worst part about it is...
3.The game gets really repetitve
This game gets WAYYY to repetitve after long amounts of time, especially near the end.
And since the game is slow paced, depending if you are good or not, you will repeat levels CONSTANTLY, to where it isn't fun anymore, and you just give up TBH.
4.The story here is GARBAGE
While I don't usually care about stories in games, the story here is AWFUL. PERIOD.
The game tries to be cool with different sections trying to be "Disturbing" Or try to have spooky moments equivelent to a creepypasta written by a 12 year old who has no idea how to make a good horror story, and thinks that sonic.exe is the spookiest thing he has ever seen.
But the biggest problem with this game is.....
5.The price
After all I have shown you, all I have talked to you about, EVERY SINGLE LITTLE THING HERE.
The game costs 24.99
With only 3-4 hours of worthwhile content with a premise that has been done better by other games, a cookie cutter "Spooky" story, Repetitve Gameplay, and only three different things to play.
It costs 24.99
Welcome to the games industry
Synopsis: Overall, Superhot is a game that has a unique and innovative concept that hasn't been done very notably in almost half a decade, and takes what could have been awesome and throws it in the trash with a huge lack of content, that content only lasting you for about 6 to 7 hours, A story that is equivelent to a creepypasta made by a 12 year old, repetitive gameplay, and a outragous price tag of almost 30 dollars, which I could use to buy shadow of mordor, game of the year edition, for 20 DOLLARS, and use that other 5 dollars to buy another great title.
Overall if you are thinking about buying this game, Don't do it
If you want to buy it really bad, wait for it to go on sale
Overall Score?
The game costs 24.99
And is really worth $ 5 dollars
If you find it at that price and are still interested, then go right ahead.
EDIT:If i have to be honest though, don't buy this game. There are much better games out there that have done this concept so much better in execution and have done it so much more justice than this game.

Banished is a strange game. It has a great aesthetic - especially in the winter - that is compelling enough to keep you coming back for more. There's nothing quite like the sight of your little village covered in a blanket of snow, smoke billowing  out of every chimney. Aesthetic, however, isn't really enough to hold your focus for too long. Other reviews go into great detail about what you need to do to succeed but it can be summed up in two parts - gather resources and breed.
At first this can be a fun balancing act to play out. Too much breeding and you're resources will start to dry up fast, too little and you'll struggle to get those resources quick enough to sustain your population much less grow it. Once you find the happy medium that works for your village you can plug along fairly well, at least for a while. Banished is big on throwing natural disasters at you - or at least it was for me. In three consecutive playthroughs I had things moving along wonderfully when a tornado would touch down and level my town. My population was decimated and despite my best efforts all three towns eventually died out.
Overall, that's the issue with Banished. It's not so much a city builder so much as it's a city survival game. The AI doesn't help, either, as citizens of your town can be frustratingly foolish. More than once I watched a citizen wander into the forest looking for food only to starve to death out in the wilderness when there was a surplus of food sitting in the barn for them. An even worse example for you: I once had a town starve to death despite it being flushed with productive farms. Over half of my population were farmers, herdsman, and fishermen and they still somehow found a way to starve to death, all of them. There's nothing more bleak and yet ironic than watching a farmer harvest his crops, the only person residing in a town of once over 50, slowly starving to death. And rest assured, the farmer died just like all of his friends and family, starving to death in the middle of his field.Throw a tornado or fire in on top of that, leveling a perfectly good town in its prime, and the game can become painfully frustrating.
Banished is not a bad game but like most of the reviews on here, I'll tell you the truth - there's not a lot to it. You can build a sprawling metropolis if you want but there's nothing to do with it. There's no end-game, nothing to strive for beyond trying to surive as long as possible. You can't go out and get revenge on the town that kicked out your founders or even interact with other villages. Your only contact to the outside world are solitary traders, the only evidence of life outside of your village. This game could be easily be cast as settling another planet for the first time, it's that empty. If you can get it on sale for cheap, buy it. It is fun at first and, like I said, can be beautiful in a quaint, colonial kind of way. Just understand that after a while it will lose its spice.

One of the best games on steam.
It seems to be heavily inspired by Mario, it's just as much fun as a Mario game, and it's even just as high quality. I honestly didn't expect much going into this. I thought it would just be another game that got extremely positive reviews just because people were excited, but I was wrong. This definitely deserves the praise it has been given. It has the best options menu i have ever seen, it has a few options to encourage and assist speedruns, it has flawless level design that utilises your abilties perfectly, it gives you new abilites at the perfect pace to keep things interesting, the bosses are amazing in every way, the abilites you get are all unique and fun to use, the worlds are very lively and lovable, most characters have voice acting which has been done very well, and to top it all off the visuals are amazing.
One final point, the story is perfect, and I wish a lot more games did it like this. It gives you the context as to what your end goal is and what you need to do to get there, and then just sends you on your way. Every so often, usually after accomplishing something significant, there will be a small cutscene to develop the story further. This game understands that the story isn't necessary in a game like this, so it doesn't let it interrupt the game itself, which is what the important thing is. It gives you a little bit so you understand the game, but thats it. A lot of games i have played are either heavily dominated by the story, present the story in a bad way, or neglect the story too much. This game does it perfectly though. This game has done so many things well, some of which are often overlooked in games, and I really hope the game gets the recognition it deserves for that.
If you like games of this genre, I definitely recommend buying this.
No matter your favored genre of games, if you play them then you must play this one, which will be forever mentioned in gaming history.

LIMBO is everything an indie game should be. Today, games are often made simply because they will sell. Games with huge budgets, top-notch graphics, and the most advanced AI can make millions of dollars and yet only provide the player with a lifeless experience. LIMBO puts you in a world that is devoid of color, music, and narrative and yet proves to be entertaining, challenging, and able to invoke emotion in the player.
LIMBO is a puzzle-platformer with very simple controls. It doesn't give you a tutorial or hold your hand. It drops you in a lonely and hostile environment and let's you figure out for yourself how to advance and how to survive. The controls are tight and the puzzles are creative and challenging without being too frustrating. You'll never be scratcing your head for too long and finding the solution to a puzzle is always satisfying. Some may complain about the trial and error process of dying and retrying. I felt that this helped to enrich the dark atmosphere with a genuine sense of peril which is very important to the game. From beginning to end, the player feels a sense of helplessness. Even though our protagnist is silent, we can sense that he is lost and confused by his hostile surroundings. This makes the need to solve puzzles all the more necessary to the player as these small victories are what drive the player to move forward and discover the secrets of this strange and beautiful black-and-white world.
10/10

This is possibly the best experience you will have with a post-apocalyspe genre. This game has so many features in its early version. There are hundreds of different items and foods. Tools, weapons, and materials can be used to create entire buildings up to several stories tall. There is a simple crafting system allowing you to use improvised weapons and tools as well. You can get trapped on the second story of a building and be trapped by a ravenous horde controlling the first floor. You can choose to risk your health and life to jump out the window and make your dashing escape with or without injury...or you can rip off the curtains and tie them into a rope stable enough to lower yourself down and out of the infested building. Scavenging a local house you can open a closet to find a zombie who then rushes you and sinks his teeth into your neck. Several in-game items have no purpose even when they look useful and several items and weapons have placeholder icons or textures. Planned and promised features are aplenty such as vehicles and NPCs. Brilliant zombie game. Blends survival, (real survival) action, simulation, RPG mechanics and of course, zombies. While the zombie genre has been over used to death, (just like that pun) this game really brings something fresh. The greatest aspect is the certainty that you WILL DIE. The real question is when.
Graphics
The graphics are pleasing for me, the style mixes really well and nothing ever sticks out of place except bugs in the art and lighting. The developers are costantly working on this though.
Map
The map is set out realisticly and has many locations including lumber yards, farms, wilderness, houses, shops, motels, and more. It is important to mention here that the world is NOT procedurally generated. I think this is good because it makes the world feel far more real and considering how big the developers plan the world to be - it's not going to be a problem.
Gameplay
If you love survival games, this game will be perfect for you. You can play heaps of different ways and even allows for the "run and gun" tactics which will definitly lead to an untimely end. The developers do stress that if you want to survive long term, you must stay down, sneak around zombies and avoid running - for one scratch could mean zombification. You must keep healthy, scavenge supplies, eat, drink, craft, explore, barricade and heaps more. Keep in mind these are slow zombies, and is tailored for a Romero audience. While you can play sandbox mode and set the zombies to sprinters, this is extremley challenging due to all the other factors you have to survive too,
Planned
There are many planned features, including multiplayer, vehicles, an even larger map, hunting and far far more. I suggest you check the forums for planned features.
Gripes
The only major gripes I have with this game in its current state is the occasional graphical glitches which can really take you out of the game. Another gripe is the UI glitches. They have recently given their UI an overhaul, and while the new inventory system is amazing, some of the pop up menu's look glitchy.
Verdict
This game has the potential to be incredible, even in its current state I could sink hours into it (and have), my lack of game time on my profile is due to me backing this game back in 2011 and I have played many hours of the non-steam version. So, if you love survival zombie games and have a solid zombie apocalypse plan that you want to put into action, this is the game for you.

Well this mod fixes it and oh guess what. Machine guns actually kill!! With this mod i have torn thousands of infintry squads apart with just ONE machine gun, where as before i had to have two bunkers just to rout them with hardly no damage done.
The mod doesn't just change Machine guns, it also changes damage, armor value, etc. of tanks. The panther now can stand against a lousy Stuert without getting penetrated somehow by it's gun. It's not just the panther that has a change, the King Tiger is nearly invincible to most fire (Except a Firefly from what i've noticed.)
To put it short, it's no longer who has patience, it's who have the bigger stick. Meaning it's about using cover effectively and not charging 2 ft in front of your enemy and absolutely dominating.

The best part of this game is the fight against the elements: the cold, the hunger, the dark.  Getting stuck in a fish-hut on a frozen lake in a seemingly endless cycle of blizzards and blinding, heavy fog. Getting lost in the forest in the middle of the night when you're only 500 meters from home but you can't remember which way you came from.
It's very satisfactory to craft better clothing from deer hides and rabbit fur. To find medicinal plants. To find a cave that protects you from the icy wind and make a lifesaving fire. Then make a nice, hot herbal tea that revitalizes you.
The art style is beautiful and evocative. There's much to explore: forests, lakes and mountains, settlements, abandoned mines and highways.
And then there are the wolves. They ruin everything. Your clothes, and your fun. Fortunately, you can play on a mode called Pilgrim where the wolves (and the bears) don't attack you, so you can focus on survival rather than stealth.
The game is quite stable and runs well.
In sandbox mode there is a lack of positive goals, but there is a story mode still to come.

I played this game on a livestream for October during a spooky week. I must say this game is definately worth playing. I have also played through the DLC. I chose to play on the lowest difficulty (new to horror games and Outlast in general).
First impressions of the game were good, the graphics were above average for games of a similar price range. However it was clear the developers had chosen to put more focus into other elements of the game (explained later). Moving through the game I thought the storyline was well thought out, interesting and flowed well. The game's story felt cohesive and structured. The documents and recordings added an extra layer of interactivity which I thought was nicely crafted providing more information for those curious such as myself. The story explored the theories of human ethics and insanity in a very interesting way. For me the standout point for this particular game had to be the music/sfx. I felt these sold the game and made the situations and tension much greater, they were also a good audio indicator of what was about to happen in the game such as a chase or exploring with a variant wandering. I thought the monsters were again, above average, I like the fact it didn't become too "fantasy" and the developers didn't get too carried away. I thought the Waldrider was an excellent choice for the overall protagonist. I definately enjoyed the element of progression you could feel as you explored the Aslyum. My one real drawback with this game and it has been something I've noticed in other games is in sections it can become a little difficult determining where you need to go, especially during chases where you don't have much time to make a snap decision, and on a blind through it lead for me to a lot of unfortunate deaths. I thought in sections the game did this really well through the use of trails of blood and making important objects glow, but I feel hidden doors, shelves, vents etc. could have been made more obvoius in sections by either using more of the blood trails or making them glow, perhaps a tradeoff in the lower difficulties.
For the DLC, I have pretty much a similar opinion, I liked the approach they took exploring a different character but rather than portraying them at a different time period such as a prequel using the same time and enviroments we were already familiar with from the main game was a nice touch. I thought again the storyline for the DLC was good, and just the right length, both the DLC and the main game didn't drag out like some games can do. Overall it was a good experience, worth the cost I paid and definately repays its value. The game does have an element of replay value in the sense that you can return for harder difficulties, collecting all the notes/documents etc. and more. Overall I'd say this is a worthwhile purchase not only for streamers but also for anyone interested in the horror genre of video games.

I like the trading system changes, or what I've seen of them so far. It adds some depth to the trading, which is something I didn't know Tropico needed until now.
I like the snap-to-grid effect when placing buildings/roads. It makes it a bit easier to set up your island.
Cons
I don't like the overlay system. It is hard to see underneath all the trees. It looks nice, but personally I find it just makes it hard to judge where to drop ranches/plantations/etc.
I don't like the amount of gated content. There is the research gating (which is fine on its own) and the war requirement gating (which is annoying and unnecessary in a lot of cases). Obviously, the war gating makes sense historically most of the time. In-game, I think the amount of content gated by the wars is a bit extreme. I should be able to have a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ little clinic before the first war if I have the cash for it.
I don't like the lack of WASD camera controls. The devs did announce that they'd be implementing them soon, so its not a huge deal. It just seems like it should have been put in to begin with, as I remember quite a bit of clamoring for them in 4.
I don't like the new voice actors or characters. This is a serious issue for me. Way more serious than it is for others, I'm sure. The NPCs seem flat and bland. Even the new characters' pictures are less caricature-like than they were previously. The voice acting is sub-par compared to 4. The humor and silly voice acting were what made me fall hard for Tropico. If I had played this game first, I'd probably never try the others and I probably wouldn't play after finishing the campaigns. Seriously. I never thought I'd miss Sunny. The new Penultimo sounds like a toolbag compared to 4's. I miss Lord Chuffney.
Overall, I'm enjoying it but am I little bit disappointed at the same time. I'd like to mess around in multi-player before I can say if this game will be eating up all my free-time in the near future or not.

Red Orchestra 2 is fun like a visit to the Normandy beaches is fun - you enjoy being there but know you should not enjoy it. The same goes for RO2. The game has a high learning curve and is not easy to get in to. On top of that, the slow pace and getting killed without any notion how, make that it is not a game for everyone. This game came as a shock to me. After the let down that was Yooka-Laylee I did not have high expectations for this. But holy hell this game is a blast. Funded on just the fraction of what Yooka-Laylee was and came out far, FAR superior this game hits all the right notes.
The art is simply adorable and everywhere, even dark and dank locations pop out at you with all the right colours and designs. The music, with help from legendary composer Grant Kirkhope fits in wherever its used coming close to one of my favorite soundtracks of all time.
But beyond all else, its the gameplay that shines through. It takes everything we loved about classic platformers from the 90's and not only modernizes it but perfects it. The maps are designed in such a way where there is a clear path but if you have the know-how you can make some pretty nice shortcuts and in some cases secrets. All the hats (used as powers) are unique, though sadly it is a case of some hats are FAR more useful than others so it would have been nice to see the hats been used in more of a variety.
The only big negative I have with this game was the final boss. Great boss fight however my first encounter I had managed to hit said boss before they dashed and they just vanished. Poof. Gone. I was locked in the arena with no way to damage myself to restart or anything so I had to play through the entire stage again to get to it. I know this bug was reported back near release (earliest post I found was mid October) and it's still not fixed which sucks. This also leads me to wish they had a button to just restart the level without returning to the hub. Some achievements required you to do certain things without taking damage or within certain times etc and having to go back to hub then re-enter a stage becomes a drag.
And yes, Jontron does have a minor cameo in the game. I've seen a lot of complaints about this. And honestly, grow up. Yes, the man made a pretty big mistake, but don't punish an entire studio for his inclusion. As with a lot of celebrities, Jon Jafari himself is a bit of a♥♥♥♥♥♥ but Jontron the character is still enjoyable. Regardless of that though a minor inclusion should never put you off from a game/movie/anything. Especially when its a character that is completely ignorable (I didn't even talk to his character because its just that vague, hell, I didn't even know Jon was in it till after I played the game).
Regardless, Tl;Dr if you haven't played the game yet your doing yourself a disservice by not getting it now. Its easily the best platformer on PC and for me one of the best in recent years.

Probably one of the best survival games I've played, period. I've played it since the early days on Desura, and it's grown immensely since then. It's also one of a small number of Early Access games I'll actually endorse playing in an unfinished state.
Yeah, it's another zombie game, but it's explored routes that other zombie survival games have barely even considered. Sleep, hunger, and thirst are something you have to watch for obviously, yes, but at the same time there's also fear, pain, depression, boredom, sickness, even temperature is taken into consideration. And everything will affect your character in some way.
It has one of the most comprehensive damage systems I've ever seen. Rather than just "You've taken damage! Don't let your health hit 0!", there's more to it than that. Scratches, bites, fractures, burns, infections, and bleeding can occur in all of your limbs, requiring you to take appropriate action to treat. One time I had to barricade myself in a room to perform extensive treatment; I had a deep wound in my arm from climbing in through a broken window, complete with a glass shard stuck in my character's arm. I had to remove the glass shard with tweezers, disinfect the wound, stitch it, bandage it, and keep an eye on it in case the bandage became dirty. And while it wasn't necessary, I sterilized the bandage while I was at it. Healing is something that takes place over time- unlike other games where you heal instantaneously, you'll only get better if you take care of your injuries and rest. They can even become infected if you don't take proper care of them. It's a level of realism that I've legitimately never seen in another game, and I appreciate that they took the time to implement it.
One thing I like is that zombies are actually a threat in this game; one or two might not be so bad if you're properly armed, but a horde busting down a door when you're in a tight hallway is beyond horrifying. You can't just be a super zombie slayer like Tallahassee from Zombieland or any character from The Walking Dead; you have to be careful, observant, and patient. Busting through a door without any regard to what may be on the other side could be harmless... or you could walk straight into a dozen zombies that have already swarmed you before you can react. And once a group of zombies has you, you're done for. GG. Been nice knowing you.
Most of all though, Project Zomboid understands what it means to be a survival game. While there is multiplayer as well as single player, it's not just a PvP manhunt disguised as a surival game like DayZ. PvP does exist, but even if you are in multiplayer, more often than not you have other concerns as opposed to hunting down other players for their food (though it is possible.) It places PvE first and foremost- it's you against the world, and the world is full of dead things. And depression, and the lack of food, and houses with alarms to alert said dead things, and uncertainty, and many other things out to ruin your day and get you killed. PvP is merely an additional feature in multiplayer, and far from required.
There's so many things I could go into about this game and why it's one of the best survival games out there. Best suggestion I can give is to play it for yourself. If you're a fan of survival games, this is probably one of the most intense survival games you'll find- good enough to rival Don't Starve [Together], and that's saying something, as Don't Starve is one of the best survival games on Steam.

Where to even begin with this game.. It's been a crazy winding road, with complete 180's, flips and sharp turns.
Dungeon Defenders as an IP. Great concept, the original came out swinging.. made headlines and sold over a million copies. Dungeon Defenders 2.. lackluster from the start. Failed Moba... staff problems, then a rebuilding from the ground up to what you see in front of you now. Please do not be fooled with the hours I, or many people have put into this game. Many of these hours were spent from the "alpha to beta stage" and just a few hours into the release of this product at time of posting.
The core of the game is there, while it spent many years trying many different things from the heroes you play and their towers they place, to the enemies and items you find along the way. It's been interesting to say the least. Many restarts, buffs, and nerfs. We all felt the good and bad of this EA title. This game is now in the "stable" phase and released as a full product. With that said, this game is being updated and having content added semi-regularly, but this comes with a word of caution. Trendy has a wide swing with their patches and updates. You never know what to expect until it hits you. I've enjoyed the game more than i did spend complaining and writing my opinions on their forums.
Just like the original game. It's a solid Tower Defense game, but with a large focus on hero usage... like the end game of the original for DPS'ing down bosses. Plenty of maps to choose, lots of heroes for different play styles. You'r own ability to choose how hard or easy you wish to make the game for yourself. Plenty of varried enemies and mini bosses to slay or have annoy you. Then the big one in the room... Items and RNG to keep you playing till you really can't take it anymore.
The game is in a good place, but I question the motives of a company that starts out saying no "Pay 2 win" and goes along and adds some DLC packs with clear items to trick and confuse future players into spending money.
Example:
ABOUT THIS CONTENT
Be the Defender that Etheria needs (or deserves) with the Heroic Edition! This edition contains:
7,500 Gems to purchase Heroes, Tower Skins, Costumes and more.
The Dryad, Lavamancer and Mystic to add to your deck of heroes.
The Guardian of the Molten Citadel legendary costume for the Squire.
Legendary Katkarot Pet to finally put your power level over 9000.
--------------------------------------------

I highly reccommend this game, as I said at the start it's thought provoking and has great atmosphere. This game really makes you appreciate the things we often take for granted in our day to day lives.

Buy this if:   You want to explore a fantastically disturbing Lovecraftian world that manages a sense of a humor and a sense of wonder throughout, in the context of resource management and brutal death always over the horizon.
Explanation/Caveat:  Sunless sea sometimes gets sold as similar to FTL, or a rogue-like, but this isn't very accurate.  Permadeath is optional (and no shame in turning it off at all), first of all.  The randomization is minimal.  With full knowledge of the game, you should basically never die.  Ever.  The main draw of the game of learning about it.  Once you have, it loses much of its luster.  But it will take 30 plus hours, at the least, to get a good grasp of everything going on in the unterzee.  Unfortunately, getting more than one ending will take much longer than this, but at the least there are some branching quest lines that will keep going.  And even if you only achieve one objective...this game is still w focal point of the game is the story.  #2 is managing your resources to explore the unterzee.  #3 (and frankly a distant third) would be economic trading/combat.
Pros:
- Best writing I've read in a game since planescape torment.
- Excellent music
- Ridiculously oppressive atmosphere
- Exploration is a good mix of enlightening and frightening
- Rewarding to learn about the world you are thrust in.  Knowledge is greatly rewarded.
Cons:
- Combat is extremely simple and straightforward.
- Slow as hell.
- End game becomes a grind without the main draw of story driving the game
- Future captains involve repetition of known elements of the game.  Not a problem for the first couple, but is another long term con.  This isn't a game you could play forever like FTL.

First. I love this mod. It’s different than original. And this is good thing to begin with.
If you expect a mod with just a bunch of new units and maps, you will be disappointed. The mod changes the game mechanics so much, i would call it almost different game.
Positive:
-	Soldiers are dying fast. If your soldiers are in open field, they will die. There is no front assault on a bunker, just because you have super infantry.
-	If you hit tank from back, it does make serious damage, sometime one hit is enough. Great! No OP vehicles. From other hand – there is no way of taking down tank without proper weapons. If you don’t have some, you are done.
-	Finally trenches, sand bags, covers, bunkers, buildings – it all matters It has a sense. You have to play more defensive.
-	Bonuses matters. Experience matters. Additional weapon matters. Much more than in original game.
-	Different unit matters. There is no universal unit for everything. I happen to be using units, I had no reason to use before.
-	Artillery, bombardment, bombs – it has devastating effect. Good.
-	Guns shoot further than unit see. Great tactical option, makes much more usage of snipers, MG nests, artillery trenches and scout units.
-	There is really no mindless spamming of units. You can do that, but probably first MG or anti-tank artillery will tear you apart. You will use more units, than in original game, and they die fast, but you have to place them well to push forward.
-	Possibility to play only with infantry! Yaha!
Negative:
-	It crashes.
-	Multiplayer problems. Sometimes it just will not load, or not load some player, and so on.
-	Lag problems. Some new maps are ok, some (even smaller maps) lag as hell.
-	Command trees. There are different command trees for different maps, great. But it causes chaos. If you didn’t play the map already, you don’t know what abilities you will get. Sometime is not pleasure surprise.
-	Uniqueness of nations. I dont know if it is good or bad thing. All nation got some basic units, abilities, like commanders, some basic defensive structures, types of units, and so on.  It is nice, nations seam more balanced, but they have lost part of unique game play styles.
End verdict: For me it is different game, and its great! I recommend it a lot.

I like it. I like this old game. It was released in April 2007 with little or no fanfare. I think I may have seen this game but I never really tried it out unlock games like Guilty Gear and Street Fighter. If my guess is correct, this game never made it to the arcades. Perhaps the parent company didn't want to invest much in this game. Based on an interview I've read online, the director, Emiko Iwasaki, was not given much support as she was a female. She got only new staff and interns.
Gameplay-wise, it's like any other fighter game, light/ heavy punch/kick. Slam is punch+kick. While it doesn't have the dodge mechanic like King of Fighters or the super high jumping and partner swapping like Marvel vs Capcom, you can find similarities to the Guilty Gear series. Quarter/semi circle, punch/kick, infinite combos, etc. Standard things like shooting fireballs, dash attacks, big guy smashes, etc. Best played with a joypad.
Conclusion, do try this game. It seems incomplete but I like it. The "good olde days" of arcades are long past. It would be a good idea for games like this to rethink their business model. Fighter games are very niche and without the arcade machines providing the joystick, it would be best to look at another model of distribution and publicity.
1. Artwork
I like the style. It's the kind I like.
2. Side characters
Secoiyan, the Desert Goblin. The little bits about the exchange rate between Gobliran and World is kind of interesting.
3. Special Story Stage
Currently, I only found one such stage in Story mode for Deathbringer where you fight his doppelganger, End of Deathbringer. There's a twist where you have to use Heat mode in order to deal damage to End of Deathbringer. Sadly, it's the same thing for Ashley Loveless as well.
4 Moving Ship on the Map
Looks so cool. Something that I would have done.
1. Repeated Design
Odile is a black version of Olivia, the Princess. While it may be thematic, the carbon copy causes a drop in quality. Rather, Odile should be another character design instead.
2. Insufficient Characters
12 is definitely not enough. My gut feel is 36 characters minimum. They will be basically 3 page selections of what we can see on screen. Then each page selection is a certain class of characters. You have your damage, support and tank types. E.g. Donvalve is a tank type, big and fat.
3. Cel-Shading
I think it's called cel-shading. The 3D models of the characters look bad on-screen. It just doesn't have that Guilty Gear look.
4. Short Game Time
Fighting games tend to be very short. You can artificially extend the game time but making the stages ultra difficult but that's just bad game design. Any game company can do this. Also, increasing the difficulty beyond a certain threshold just puts players off.
5. Mirror Battles
I am talking about the Face story battle. It's really stupid to fight another carbon copy of your character. It's just lousy.
1. Storyline
It's very basic and not enticing. The formula is big bad evil vs heroes. While that is the default mode of good vs evil stories, it's missing something extra.
2. Different Storylines Depending on Character
I am not sure how to deal with this. Based on the current game, you will have different outcomes when you use different characters. This is interesting. However, this causes the game to have Storylines equal to the number of characters. In this case, there are 12 different storylines. It's like writing 12 different variations of a story. Interesting but confusing.
3. Complex Controls
I understand that this basically appeals to a certain niche of gamers. Most people can't play fighting games due to the sheer complexity and dexterity required to pull off the combos. The hand-eye coordination requires hours of practice to polish.
1. More Unique Story Mode Stages
Currently, the story stages are basically the same. You have some story overlay before and after the fight then 9 stages of bishy bashy. I would suggest giving each character their own special stage
2. Main Storyline and Congregation at Focal Point
Make just 1 main storyline with each character supporting the main storyline. At the final stage, create a reason for all the characters to congregate at one focal point. If you were to visualize this, it would look like a network of roots that criss-cross but ultimately end at one important point. This creates continuity and closure at the same time.
3. Character Lore
Honestly, some added lore would be great. You can read a character biography with background and interesting quirks about the character. This helps to fluff up the character. Stats and moves are not enough.
4. Location Lore
The places that they fight in can have little bit of lore to make it sound interesting.
5. Visual Effects To Match Voice Acting
The story overlay doesn't have the full range of emotions. It's a minor thing but you notice something odd when the voice acting sounds a certain way and the picture is the same. It throws you off a little.
6. Challenge Stages
Remember the car bashing challenge in Street Fighter 2? Or the tile breaking in Street Fighter? You need something that takes away from the constant fighting once in a while. Do not put in the beach volleyball challenge.
7. RPG-Fighting Game Hybrid
Honestly, the way the characters are designed seem more suitable for a RPG. A fighting game is great too but let's face it, any kind of character can be made into a fighting game. e.g. Dissidia, Ehrgeiz. Perhaps, ARC could try something totally novel and make a RPG-fighting game hybrid? However, you would need to dumb down the controls a lot. I believe gameplay from games like Guardian Heroes would combo well with this type of game.
8. Youtube Videos on how to do Super Combos like the Pros
Yea, in the early 2000s, Youtube wasn't so popular and Facebook was just getting started. You need to give aids to people who want to play fighting games but have no idea what to do. If you google "Battle Fantasia Guides", you will have horrible guides that use notations like 5b, j6a, etc. How would anyone understand?

Decay: The Mare is a decent, short adventure game with good story, simple puzzles and good soundtrack.
You play as Sam, who checked in a clinic to help with his drug problems: soon reality and dreams start to mix and you'll realize not everything is what it seems.
-overall interesting story with episode 3 providing good closure
-very nice piano soundtrack
-decent puzzles with mostly logical, albeit easy,solutions
-a good, eerie atmosphere
-graphics are blurry and low res: they look pretty bland and quite bad on a big screen
-interface is a bit clunky
-moving around can sometimes feel a bit limited or confusing, to make things worse when exiting certain rooms you'll be  facing the wrong way
-a few jump scares don't really work well and either feel forced or just not scary at all
-short (2 hours) and quite easy
The game started a bit slowly and Episode 1 was perhaps the least interesting of the three but as I kept playing the story became pretty interesting and I truly wanted to see how it'd end: and thankfully so since the story is Decay's only strongest point together with its soundtrack. The puzzles are decent but most are very easy and thus not much of a challenge while the graphics are poor overall with slightly pixelated cutscenes and blurry backgrounds.
I see Decay as a good purchase if you're either new to adventure games and thus looking for an easy game to learn the ropes or a more seasoned gamer looking for something easier to relax without too much hassle: everyone else can safely skip this one and look for longer and better games.
No matter what though I wouldn't spend more than the 2$ I got it for due to the very short length.

For everyone that has had issues with a black and white screen on startup!  This is to help you!
Instructions:
Find the game in your library, right click, and go to properties.  Browse the local files and find the windows 7 or windos 8 icon for the game in those files.  Whichever one you use, right click it and go to properties.  Move to the compatibility tab, and check the 'disable display scaling on dpi' and apply the settings.  This should allow you to play the game.
It worked for me, just figured I would share the knowledge before you spend hours trying to screw with your settings to fix this stupid issue.  Cheers mates!

Я взял (в своей библиотеке) эту игру на пробу, чисто чтобы разгрузить список неигранного и посмотреть очередной рогалик. Тут меня ждали два сюрприза. Во-первых - это, строго говоря, не рогалик, а паззл "с элементами". А во-вторых, игра оказалась от того же Сергея Боброва, что и Way of Gold and Steel, который я "распечатал" в то же самое время! Совпадение.
Итак, сама игра, как я уже сказал - паззл. Формально есть сюжет "узнай, что случилось с кораблём, пропавшим на другой планете", а по факту имеем повторяющийся и усложняющийся цикл задач "собери Х ресурсов, построй Y и Z и постарайся не умереть в процессе".
Честно говоря, умереть в процессе не так-то просто, как только ты поймёшь принцип действия игрушки. Во-первых, все противники достаточно тупые, и, увидев тебя, бегут напрямик. Это крайне облегчает жизнь, потому что, во-вторых, из оружия у героя есть только бомбы, реагирующие на приближение, и будь монстры чуть поумнее, дело бы неизменно заканчивалось весьма печально. И в-третьих, гибернация (необходимая по условиям игры) - очень долгий процесс, во время которого вокруг тебя генерятся мириады монстров. Так что необходимо место сна окружать непробиваемыми титановыми блоками и спать спокойно.
Кроме "активных" врагов, есть ещё и "пассивные" - радиоактивная слизь кое-где на стенках. Справиться с ней достаточно просто - убираешь блок, на котором сидит слизь, и она умирает, если не может перелезь на другой, выходящий на ту же клетку. Главное - не подхватить в процессе радиационное заражение.
Ещё есть три типа ресурсов, которые нужно добыть - а потом потратить на исследования и экипировку. Ничего сложного, но добыча - не бесплатна, а энергетические ячейки кончаются очень быстро.
Собственно, это и всё. С каждым этапом задача усложняется (карта становится больше, ресурсов для строительства надо больше, а монстры всё сильнее), но тип задачи не меняется.
Рекомендую, если уж очень хочется рогалик-головоломку. Иначе лучше пропустить.

This is gonna be a really quick (I hope) review of Decay-The Mare. . .
I'm actually in game as I write this,I just wanted to say something really fast about this game,yes,it's a point and click !! But I believe that for this game,it really works !! I personally love P&C games,they are the first type of games I played when I left the world of HOGs and started looking for a more involved genre of games to play !! Just like P&C mystery games,this game has a nice flow,so far. . . .
It seems to me to have all the ambience of a decently made horror game,you feel creeped out being in this seemingly abandoned rehab hospital. . . I like the subject of the game too,going through treatment for drug abuse,it's a bold subject and could have been taken the wrong way by the audience and could have offended A WHOLE LOT OF PEOPLE !!
I,for one,think it's an outstanding subject and I believe that there is SO MUCH that can be done with this subject matter and I'm hoping to see way more ideas about it in the future !!
O.K.,about the game itself,it's a fairly standard point and click mystery/horror game. I think the surroundings are pretty creepy,the music lends itself to the feeling of dread,it's very unobtrusive but at the same time,it's always there,in the background,quietly sending out creepy vibes !!
There is plenty to do here and plenty of places to go and doors to enter. . .I've only come across 2 mini games so far and they were pretty straightforward P&C puzzles,if you take your time and observe your surroundings you'll find the answers to the puzzles,but you do have to be diligent and pay attention-you never know what is a clue and what's put there to throw you off the scent !! I think thats one of the things I look for in this genre,I want the answers to be in the gameplay,I don't want them to be so obscure I have to resort to a walkthrough,thats not a fun game,thats a crappy made game and those are the games I delete right away !! One thing I often do with games is I take notes !! Yes,take actual handwritten notes,that I can refer back to and use in case I get stuck and am not sure what to do !
You have an inventory,accessable by the I key on the keyboard,while in the inventory you have the ability to look at everything you've collected,you can turn things around and look at the backs of things,I suggest you should do that,if they give you that option,they do it for a reason and I believe you should take full advantage it. You also have a "combine" ability while in your inventory,as with the examine ability,I believe they give us this for a reason and it's never hurt anybody to try every insane combo you can !! You never know what will work together and what will not,unless you experiment around with your items !!
I'm gonna slide back in game now,I'll repost in this review as I progress deeper in game. . .

I have been following this game for some time, since it was first shown as a Game Jam '14 entry. Instantly I thought it looked very interesting and fun. Now that the game is released and modestly fleshed out, I have to admit, I LOVE it!!
So the main mechanic is the speed of time. When you are not moving, it moves SUPER slow. When you look around, it speeds up a little. Finally, when you move, it goes into normal speed. Your object is to kill the enemies utilising these mechanics without eating a bullet, fist or blade first. It sounds simple but it is almost like a puzzle game at times when you need to figure out the order of your actions otherwise you die. You can punch dudes, grab their guns and shoot them in the head and then throw the empty gun at someone to stun them, allowing you to move in for the kill. It's great fun and SUPER satisfying.
The "story" is not too long and seems to be the main complaint amongst folk. Depending on your skill level, it can be done within a few hours. However, the game then has challenge modes which have certain criteria such as running through the levels again allowing throwing items only, punching only, one bullet per gun as well as altering the look of the game. I've put about 8 hours in so far and that includes finishing the story and completing about 1/3 of the challenges. I think the price tag is a bit much for the content provided, I believe £10-£12 would be a fairer price point.
Aside from the price, I would recommend this to anyone. It's really fun, interesting and satisfying to play. It even includes an endless mode, so there is still stuff to do after the story and challenges. It did not let me down and in fact surpassed my expectations, I only wish it lasted longer.
Buy it.

NOTE: The below review is a couple days after the initial, official release AND my impressions from a few hours of playing. I am impressed and like it even only after my first 10-12 game sessions of playing.
Superb - finally a solid turn-based lightweight strategy + luck (procedural map, creatures, etc) + rogue-like game. Good concept, design, replayability, evoking a lighter C64-ish/early PC/Flash loose variant perhaps of something like project firestart (C64); X-com (early PC); Motherload (flash mining game) in feel and simple gameplay. I am a gamer from the days of Atari thru c64 thru 90s PC to a current player of the more contemporary retro/pixel scene games looking for turn-based games of this type. There have really not been many (and good ones) out there as far as new games on contemporary platforms, going back over the past 20 years!
* LINUX-USERS: Game works fine in PlayOnLinux - simple default steam install environment, and will should run with no issue or effect on old systems concerning cpu-usage.
* GOOD DESIGN FOR CHALLENGING GAMES: Takes advantage of simple procedural design to spawn new but small maps, I assume to facilitate the end-goal task in a timely manner. From the dev response on the steam discussion thread, a skilled uber-geek gamer may be able beat the scenario in 2 hours. (Me: maybe 25-50 tries if lucky, or many hours).
* REPLAYABILITY: However, in regard to above, it's procedural so sort of a pseudo-puzzler/turned-based action game you will can replay over-and-over again. You may win an odd game session, you will probably end up quiting an impossibly difficult game, restarting, etc. I can only speculate as I justed started playing but I assume it is possible to win each game (?), but if you're like me, I know when I'm licked, and if so I will gladly restart a new game. I have spent a couple hours already (not close to beating it) and when I do finally beat it (who knows, as mentioned previously, I expect more like 15 hours or 50 tries), it's not like a crappy movie where you'll never watch it or play it again. By design this game is meant to play until you beat and then revisit now-or-later.
* TURN-BASED MAGIC: I have little time to play games or get that involved at this point in my life, but I do revel and really appreciate simple turn-based strategy or thoughtful game designs in the modern era of games. There is HUGE LACK OF TURN-BASED STRATEGY GAMES TODAY.
* RETRO-ENTHUSIASTS: good atmosphere, graphics and music evoking an authentic experience, with simple but stellar gameplay, offering -/+ scoring and fat-trimmed replayability.
* POSSIBILITY OF EXPANSION? It would be great though to have the game expanded for example either sequel/episode/level/scenario-wise where the developer could implement, balance and package additional scenarios or even another release, OR expand/update the game here in some way with even more content or options. I really think it is worth it.
* MAKE SURE TO WATCH THE TRAILER (INSTRUCTIONAL): The game once you actually understand clearly what you need to do (build a walled enclosures and then the radar AND survive), May come off not only lightweight in cpu-usage but it also in regards to a small world size/map and content/objective. But it in a nutshell it is a hybrid game meant for procedural replayability.
* WOULD LOVE NOTHING MORE THAN THIS TYPE OF GAME TO GAIN MOMENTUM AND BE EXPANDED AND BUILT FURTHER ON (FOR SUPPORTERS LIKE ME!) AS THE STEAM PLATFORM CAN ALLOW THAT TO HAPPEN. First impression may be for some people that it's too small or simple (ps. difficult options are present, and easy seems hard enough to me), but that is besides the point and of the challenge and design of the game. BUT I would hardly complain and wish there will be expansion or some kind of sequel. But as it is, I am very glad to have this in my game library and will be a game that I will pop in my disk drive for awhile to come! Well worth the affordable, full initial price. Well done.

Cuphead is a run and gun side scrolling shooter/platformer with a focus on tough diverse bosses, the game immediately hooks you in with its 1930's cartoon style visuals, sounds and direction. It certainly is what captured my attention many years ago at E3 and I was very impressed with the final product.
Whilst I wouldn't really say there is a story as such there is a plot in cuphead, brothers cuphead and mugman have found themselves in debt to none other than the devil himself. Forced into a contract of debt the brothers must fight for their very souls whilst gathering the souls of those who are in debt to the devil in order to save themselves from a lifetime of servitude.
Which is where the boss fights come in, they are the main focus of the game and they don't disappoint. Each boss's soul is required to progress and each boss must also be defeated on the harder difficulty to access the final parts of the game which may be a throw off to some. The game has platforming elements but is mostly a side scrolling run and gun, enemy's attack in non stop waves and in many cases spawn infinitely never giving you a moment to rest. The game will give you 3 (upgradeable to 5) lives for each level, once they are lost its game over and there is no way to regain health or respawn (at least in single player) so skill and knowledge of each level is essential. There aren't many games that give me that wonderful sense of satisfaction and accomplishment upon defeating a boss like cuphead does and oh it feels good.....however. I would have to say I died well over 400 times throughout my playthrough (theres a counter) and it goes without saying that you will die a lot in this game. A lot. But endure through, push hard and theres a light at the end of the tunnel.
The biggest part of this game is the visuals and it does not let you down, each boss and area is completely different and unique and I can say that no 2 are the same. Theres a sense of modern wit combined with that classic 1930s technicolor film style and comedy that makes Cuphead stand tall. I can't imagine how much work went into each individual hand drawn watercolour paintings but it certaintly isn't something I've seen before, I would love to see perhaps another game by the same studio in the same style but a more traditional platformer?
Sound is all original jazz and swing recordings that is very pleasant to my ears, especially as a fan of the era and music of old and big bands.
In closing I highly recommend this game to all gamers not just those looking for a challenge or the hardcores, Cuphead is a breath of fresh life and deserves to be played.

CONCLUSION:
Almost a good game, fun for a few hours, but lack of content + AI flaws leave you feeling like it's a beta that the developers never finished.
FULL Review:
Banished is a casual sandbox city-builder. There is no story, multiplayer, nor endgame, so "casual" really is its true nature. Remniscent of Age of Empires, you begin the game with a few settlers and modest supplies and must build structures and assign jobs to gain more food, wood, stone, and other resources to grow your town.
Unlike Age of Empires:
-you will never be attacked, so there's no combat buildings
-there aren't any varieties of civilizations, so every playthrough will offer the same "city"
-there isn't a technology tree
-the most notable difference: in Banished, you do not assign specific tasks to individual citizens, but rather you control your town as an overview-manager. For example, to build your first farm you would place a building site somewhere on the map, then go to your job-assignment window and raise your number of "builders" to 1 or 2.  Then 1 or 2 townspeople will automatically gather the necessary resources from your storage pits and go the the building site.  Then you raise your number of "farmers" to 1, and one random citizen automatically begins growing crops on the new plot.
This seems like a fun mechanic at first, but the AI is so unintuitive that it eventually becomes frustrating. Over and over, I watched my woodcutter walk all the way to the farthest storage pit in the settlement to deliver his firewood, rather than the pit right next his cutting station. Obviously, while he's walking, no new firewood is being chopped. My families were freezing. The town health and happiness were dropping. I wanted to command him to turn around and chop more wood, but in Banished you cannot control individuals. I wanted to de-assign him as the woodcutter and assign someone else who was already close to the woodcutting station, but in Banished, you cannot control individuals. All you can do is set your number of woodcutters to the maximum of "1". The AI handles the rest. There were countless other examples of AI flaws (see other reviews): buildings that would never get completed, while citizen after citizen walked right by; crops that wouldn't get harvested; mines that would sit vacant.
The real deal breaker: lack of content.
After about five hours, I had built every structure in the game (around 20), assigned every corresponding job, acquired all the available crop seeds (around 12) and farm animals (3). Then what? The lack of diversity left me feeling like this was a game that should have been about five times as large, but for whatever reason, the developers stopped working on it. I would've loved the option of gradiated buildings that scale with your resources, like a level 1 brewery, level 2 brewery, and level 3 brewery, or some purely aesthetical options (of which there are none) to personalize my town, like gardens, fences, sculptures, etc...?
I want to recommend this game. It was fun for a few hours while I struggled through the first few winters. But with so many good games available these days, I can't justify recommending $20 for an abandoned sand-box.

Buy this if:   You want to explore a fantastically disturbing Lovecraftian world that manages a sense of a humor and a sense of wonder throughout, in the context of resource management and brutal death always over the horizon.
Explanation/Caveat:  Sunless sea sometimes gets sold as similar to FTL, or a rogue-like, but this isn't very accurate.  Permadeath is optional (and no shame in turning it off at all), first of all.  The randomization is minimal.  With full knowledge of the game, you should basically never die.  Ever.  The main draw of the game of learning about it.  Once you have, it loses much of its luster.  But it will take 30 plus hours, at the least, to get a good grasp of everything going on in the unterzee.  Unfortunately, getting more than one ending will take much longer than this, but at the least there are some branching quest lines that will keep going.  And even if you only achieve one objective...this game is still w focal point of the game is the story.  #2 is managing your resources to explore the unterzee.  #3 (and frankly a distant third) would be economic trading/combat.
Pros:
- Best writing I've read in a game since planescape torment.
- Excellent music
- Ridiculously oppressive atmosphere
- Exploration is a good mix of enlightening and frightening
- Rewarding to learn about the world you are thrust in.  Knowledge is greatly rewarded.
Cons:
- Combat is extremely simple and straightforward.
- Slow as hell.
- End game becomes a grind without the main draw of story driving the game
- Future captains involve repetition of known elements of the game.  Not a problem for the first couple, but is another long term con.  This isn't a game you could play forever like FTL.

Earl’s Access Burgers:
I’m hungry… I drive by a new burger joint that just opened up and decided to give it a try. “Hi Earl!” I proclaim, “I enjoyed a burger at your dad’s old place, Jeff’s Done Burgers, and I was looking into purchasing a delicious burger from you today! Just give me that delicious hamburger whenever you can Earl, no rush” Earl takes my order and I pay him the $14.99 up front for my soon to be burger. Earl promptly supplies me with a plate with two buns and lettuce and pleads that he just needs a little more time… I wait patiently.
Time passes… boredom onsets… and Earl finally emerges from the back with a strange cocky grin on his face. He has two new plates with him this time that have onion and cheese on one and tomato and pickle on the other. I say “Oh great Earl, we are about ready for my burger huh?,” Earl replies “ Well actually, I took a break from cooking the burger and prepared these delicious additions to go along with your burger.”I admit,  it feels slightly odd that Earl stopped working on the burger to work on these sides to go on the burger, I accept anyways. I reach out to grab these items from the plate as Earl’s hand swiftly smacks my hand away in a pompous anger as he explains… ” Sorry sir, both of these additions to your burger will be another $6.99 each.” I argue with Earl that I have already paid for the idea of a completed burger in advance, how can you say these are supplementary items when I have not yet received what I paid for to begin with?
Earl retreats to the back with both plates in hand as I sit confused and with a feeling of being taken advantage of.  I stare out the window, it begins to rain… minutes turn into hours….the storm clears… how long have I been waiting for this burger??
Earl explodes from the back, shouting and proclaiming that he has made the ultimate burger and proceeds to put up posters all over the store to show off his burger making skills. He then stops at my table, takes my plate with the bun and lettuce and throws it in the trash. With a giant grin he then says “I have made the ultimate burger it is delicious! I am so generous that I will provide you this burger, free of charge!” Earl then sets down a plate with only the burger patty on it. I look up at him in bewilderment… “What is this Earl?” Earl then explains his new business model for his store “FREE BURGER PATTIES FOR ALL! You can then buy separately every side item that you want to go with your burger and not pay for the sides you don’t want!”
Earl swats away my hand again as I reach out for the side items to complete my burger… “Sorry sir but with this new business model, you will need to individually pay for every side.” I argue with Earl that I have already paid for a completed burger and not only did he not deliver what he promised, but what I already paid for and am rightfully due.
We argue and yell… I ask Earl “You know what, forget it! I would just like my money back Earl!”  Earl replies “Sorry sir, you have waited too long in this store to qualify for a refund.” I now have exceeded my patience and at this moment I don’t even give a s^%t about this burger anymore and I storm off to my car and leave for home… hungry, disappointed and angry.
On the way to work on the following day, I drive by Earl’s Access Burgers and to my surprise, it has gone up in flames over night. Greatly no one was injured in the blaze of beef and wood. The discount shoe store and Hispanic bakery now look lonely with no establishment between them. After the initial shock of the building I just spent so much time in being completely gone, a strange smirk appears across my lips and a flutter of joy washes over me. I realize that the restaurant industry as a whole will not miss Earl’s Access Burgers and with its demise, be all the better for it.
Leave this industry Earl… you are a greedy pestilence and you set the entire industry back with your actions.

Fun Tower Defense + Shooter hybrid, DD2 is a major graphical update to the first game that I loved. It is a F2P and has a revamped campaign that is definitely worth running through, and even features a great Terraria tie in so you can play as the Dryad and maybe enjoy watching a 3d boss from the game wreak havoc.
However, after half a year of being released, I am changing my recommend to "No" on this game. The campaign is still fine so run through that if you want, but then run far far away.
The game suffers from years old major bugs that affect later game modes significantly (monsters getting stuck in spawn points, monsters ignoring walls, etc) and an expanding list of design decisions that the majority of the community keep fighting (no chance to pick what map you play  after campaign, maddening insistence on keep nerfing your hero to progress (through Mastery and Power of the Ancients), plainly broken (or just dumb) loot system, frustrating enemies like assassins that just warp on top of you and immobolize you, monster immunity in spawn points, etc etc). The game was release with many many known major bugs and no end game, and after 6 months end game was delivered in a form that the majority of the players just hated while years old bugs still happen. It is bad enough having the bugs in normal modes where you may just get an objective hurt that shouldn't, but with Mastery and PotA that easily causes a loss that will set you back hours of game time.
After the Terraria update in late 2016, the updates have had some good ideas that have all been flawed so badly that it just drove players away. After a year of this, it is just time to admit that it isn't going to get fun. Player base has gone done 75% in a year and 90% since their peak in 2015, so think hard before spending real money on an online only game that can fold at any time.

Decay - The Mare has very little substance to it.
The game style is a point- and-click puzzle horror adventure. Your character is a psychiatric patient who thinks he's woken up during the night  but then finds he is in a medicine induced nightmare that he can't seem to escape. The gameplay consists of single clicks to move around, open doors, pick up objects and solve puzzles.
The people who will like this game are those who really like sudden scares. The game is full of doors slamming shut in your face, shadowy figures running on the periphery of your vision, objects being thrown at you by invisible forces... that sort of thing. If you're happy to turn the lights down, walk around an old creepy building and have things go BOO! at you, then buy the game.
If is is important to you that your games have interesting plots, interesting characters, good scripting or challenging puzzles this isn't for you.
More detail:
There is a consistent plot arc running through the three chapters which is completed without leaving many things unexplained but it lacks any detail.
The puzzles are really lacking. Most involve taking undisguised codes from one part of the environment to open a door in another. I found nothing challenging and therefor not satisfying.
Any creepy atmosphere the game might have generated was ruined by the horrible navigation mechanism. The same icon is at different times used to move you back a step, make you turn around 180 degrees or  move you back a step followed by turning around 180 degrees. It's disorientating and tedious.  It was annoying enough to stop any spooky atmosphere coming through.
